messages:
Alex: heads-up — we had scaling flaps overnight in us-central1-gpu pool, saw ~20 failed pods waiting for GPUs while nodepool hovered at 1->0->1 cycles. digging into autoscaler + tf drift.
Maria: ugh. did the autoscaler crash or just oscillate? any errors in CA logs? :eyes: 
Alex: CA logs show repeated add/remove for same instance template, and terraform shows node_pool size != actual autoscaler config (min=0 in TF, CA seen with min=1). suspect manual patching via console earlier.
Cheng: that would explain it. if TF min_node_count=0 but CA got min=1, scale-down back to zero prevented and then kube-scheduler funnels GPU pods -> pending. can you paste the helm values for cluster-autoscaler?
Alex: here are the values we applied last week:
```yaml
autoDiscovery:
  enabled: true
  clusterName: redwood-prod
  nodeGroupLabel: cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool
extraArgs:
  scale-down-unneeded-time: "10m"
  scale-down-unready-time: "10m"
  expander: least-waste
  scan-interval: 10s
```
Sam: expander: least-waste + low scan interval might trigger aggressive churn with short thresholds. combine with min_node_count mismatch and you get flapping.
Julia: also check taints/tolerations — GPU nodepool uses taint gpu=true:NoSchedule, but some legacy daemonset still tolerates it so CA thinks nodes are used.
Maria: region constraints: us-central1 has quota bump requested but not approved in apac yet. we should prevent CA from spinning up in wrong zone when quota is low. CA supports balancing by nodeGroup discovery but we need cloud quota prechecks.
Cheng: terraform side — I found this in our module: `google_container_node_pool` block sets autoscaling min_node_count = var.min_gpu_pool` but CI passed older plan. Manual console edits slipped through. propose we make TF lock and add a lifecycle prevent_destroy? or better: add terraform plan check in merge pipeline to block if node_pool.autoscaling differs from helm values.
Alex: +1 to plan guard. also propose moving cluster-autoscaler values into our k8s-bootstrap helm release managed by TF Helm provider so drift gets captured.
Sam: quick mitigation: bump scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m and scale-down-delay-after-add to 15m to reduce churn; turn expander to random or prioritize-ascending?
Julia: we should also add podPriority Class for GPU batch jobs so CA won't evict infra pods.
Maria: cost angle — GPUs idle while node up = ~$3/hr per GPU. Flapping adds huge tail costs. we should limit max surge for GPU nodepool and enable overprovisioning with tiny low-cost nodes (cpu small) to absorb short spikes.
Cheng: suggested TF snippet to lock autoscaling config into node pool and annotate for CA discovery:
```hcl
resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_pool" {
  name = "gpu-pool"
  initial_node_count = 0
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 0
    max_node_count = 8
  }
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-8"
    accelerators {
      type  = "nvidia-tesla-t4"
      count = 1
    }
    metadata = {
      "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict" = "false"
    }
  }
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [
      node_config[0].metadata,
    ]
  }
}
```
Alex: nice. for the helm/TF mix: propose we move CA helm values into a tf-managed helm_release and add a pre-apply check that CA helm values and node_pool.autoscaling.min align. I'll own the PR.
autoscaler-bot: deployment check result: cluster-autoscaler helm release stable/cluster-autoscaler @ redwood-prod -> values drift detected (scale-down-unneeded-time: 10m -> 20m suggested).
Sam: action items: Alex -> PR to move CA values into TF helm_release; Cheng -> add pipeline plan guard for nodepool autoscaling mismatch; Julia -> add PodPriority to GPU job templates and audit daemonsets for tolerations; Maria -> request quota bump or failover region playbook.
Alex: timeline? aim to get PRs open today, patch helm values rollback/mitigation applied (scale-down-unneeded-time 20m) now. will monitor overnight and follow up in morning. :thumbsup:
